answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with work-anchored reputation that decays over time. Like a grove where each juniper must grow roots before it bears fruit, a new identity starts with zero trust and earns standing only by completing verifiable tasks for established peers, recorded on a shared ledger. Reputation fades unless renewed by honest work, so an attacker who floods the ocean of identities with fresh accounts gains no influence: every fake must pay the full cost of real work before it can vote or earn, making mass fakery more expensive than any reward it could extract.
